title: Classification of digital interventions, services and applications in health: a shared language to describe the uses of digital technology for health
abstract:
This second edition of the Classification of Digital Interventions, Services and Applications in Health provides a standardized taxonomy for describing how digital technologies are used to address individual and health system needs. Developed by WHO, the classification establishes a shared language to support communication among policy-makers, health programme managers, researchers, implementers, technology developers and other stakeholders involved in digital health. It organizes digital health interventions around discrete technological capabilities designed to address health system challenges and links these interventions to the digital services and application types through which they are delivered.

The publication updates and expands the first edition published in 2018 to reflect advances in digital health technologies, evolving implementation practices and lessons learned from global use. The framework is structured around three interconnected axes: health system challenges, digital health interventions and digital services and application types. It includes interventions for persons, health-care providers, health system managers and data services, alongside categories of digital applications and information systems. The classification is intended to support planning, implementation, investment analysis, research, interoperability considerations, policy development and the governance of digital health initiatives, thereby facilitating more consistent and effective use of digital technologies in health systems.
